item.title: Malwarebytes Launches 50% Off Black Friday Sale Across Subscriptions
item.description:
Malwarebytes Launches 50% Off Black Friday Sale Across Subscriptions

Malwarebytes has launched its 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale, dubbed “Block Friday,” offering 50% off security subscriptions for individuals, families, and small businesses. The promotion includes discounts on antivirus software, VPNs, identity theft protection, and personal data removal services.

⚙️ Individual Plans

Individual subscriptions provide protection for three devices with varying levels of security features:

  • Standard: Antivirus, anti-malware, scam protection, and ad blocking. Discounted from $59.99 to $29.99 per year.
  • Plus: All Standard features plus a no-log VPN. Discounted from $79.99 to $39.99 per year.
  • Essential: Device security, a VPN, and identity theft protection with $1 million in insurance coverage for one adult. Discounted from $129.99 to $64.99 per year.
  • Ultimate: Device security, a VPN, identity theft protection with $2 million in insurance coverage, three-bureau credit monitoring, and personal data removal for one adult. Discounted from $279.99 to $139.99 per year.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Family Plans

  • Standard Family: Antivirus, anti-malware, scam protection, and ad blocking. Discounted from $119.99 to $59.99 per year.
  • Plus Family: All Standard Family features plus a no-log VPN. Discounted from $149.99 to $74.99 per year.
  • Essential Family: Device security, a VPN, and identity theft protection with $1 million in insurance coverage for two adults and 10 children. Discounted from $199.99 to $99.99 per year.
  • Ultimate Family: Device security, a VPN, identity theft protection, $2 million in insurance coverage, three-bureau credit monitoring, and personal data removal for two adults. Discounted from $399.99 to $199.99 per year.

💼 Small Business Plans

#Malwarebytes #CyberSecurity #BlackFriday #Antivirus #VPNServices

item.title: Google Patents My Channel: AI-Generated Personalized Videos
item.description:
Google Patents My Channel: AI-Generated Personalized Videos

Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that aims to create personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements using user data. The patent has been rejected, but the company may appeal or resubmit an amended version.

🔍 Overview

My Channel is designed to generate feeds filled with personalized content based on information Google knows about its users. First spotted by Patentlyze, the patent — filed last May and published last week — describes a system that uses demographic data and viewing history to create prompts fed into an LLM for generating AI videos tailored to individual interests.

🧩 How it works

The system would capture contextual data from users’ devices, including IP addresses, GPS locations, and age details. It could also base prompts on current news like sports scores and social media activity, with all video generation occurring on Google’s servers.

⚙️ Key details

  • Create entire movies of various genres
  • Connect to other streaming services for more user data and training content
  • Generate digital avatars of users to serve as protagonists in AI-generated content

According to the patent, if a user watches many videos about Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, My Channel might produce content similar to Ash Koosha’s Odysseus: The Fall.

#Google #AI #Patents #MyChannel #VideoGeneration

Source: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future

item.title: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus faces backlash over undiscovered AI music
item.description:
The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus faces backlash over undiscovered AI music

The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music. The controversy centers on a Grand Theft Auto-themed section where audio files contained Suno metadata pointing back to tracks on Suno’s site.

🔍 Discovery

Reddit user ShweetsStuff found several audio files embedded in the game with Suno metadata, directly linking them to Suno’s platform and the tracks heard during the GTA parody segment.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Review-bombing occurred on Steam following the discovery
  • Valve requires developers to disclose how and when they use generative AI in the development process
  • Nicalis, Inc., the studio behind Repentance Plus, did not disclose the AI music usage anywhere
  • Creator Edmund McMillen claimed he “had no idea” AI music was used in the latest version
  • McMillen took to X to apologize for the inclusion
  • Within hours of the discovery, Nicalis shared on X that Repentance Plus had been updated and the generated music files had been removed
  • Reviews have yet to rebound; the game remains rated as “overwhelmingly negative” on Steam
  • Users on X appear to be giving McMillen the benefit of the doubt, likely because he has been outspoken on AI in game development, calling it “uninspired and bland” in a TikTok from 2024

#BindingOfIsaac #AImusic #Steam #gameDev #Suno #EdmundMcMillen

Source: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus

item.title: Apple Tests Daily Usage Limits for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence Features
item.description:
Apple Tests Daily Usage Limits for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence Features

Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3, using the updates to test new per-device daily usage limits for select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features.

🧩 How it works

Basic Siri commands and requests remain free and unlimited. However, advanced features relying on cloud-based processing are subject to daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage:

  • Using Siri AI for multi-step, personal context requests
  • Image generation and editing tools
  • Automations in Shortcuts that rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models
  • Third-party apps that use those same cloud models

Apple has not specified exactly how many times these features can be used before limits are reached, noting that limits will vary based on the task. The company plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and when they have finally reached it.

⚙️ Key details

Frequent users of these features will require an iCloud Plus subscription to avoid limits. Instead of waiting until midnight for usage to reset, most existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) include higher daily limits at the same price:

Plan Monthly Cost Usage Multiplier
200GB $2.99 2x
2TB $9.99 5x
6TB $29.99 10x
12TB $59.99 20x

Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that is used on a first-come, first-served basis.

#Apple #Siri #AppleIntelligence #iCloud #UsageLimits

Source: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions

item.title: Google Maps adds AI trip planning and appointment finding via Ask Maps
item.description:
Google Maps adds AI trip planning and appointment finding via Ask Maps

Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries and provide real-time details about each stop. The update is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app.

🧩 How it works

The AI-powered Ask Maps feature can suggest stops for your next trip while providing real-time details about each location. Users can plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days. For example, Google states that you can use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping or create a schedule for a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. From there, Ask Maps generates a day-by-day schedule with a list of stops, showing your route and numbered pins for each location on the map.

⚙️ Key details

  • You can share the itinerary with friends or family members.
  • You can export the itinerary to Google Docs on desktop.
  • You can ask Maps to show your trip schedule before you leave or select the “itinerary” badge in your chat history.
  • Google Maps displays real-time information about traffic and a location’s hours alongside directions.
  • The “know before you go” details include parking, car charging, weather conditions, potential delays, and tolls during your trip.
  • Ask Maps can find specific beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments and call the locations for you.
  • You can find saved places on your list by asking queries like, “Which spots on saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”

🚀 Availability

Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Trip-planning and saved list search are rolling out to the more than 200 countries where Ask Maps is available. The “know before you go” tips and appointment-finding features are launching in the US to start.

#GoogleMaps #AskMaps #AItourism #TripPlanning #Google

Source: Google Maps can now create trip itineraries for you

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Duet, a consumer‑friendly AI work assistant
item.description:
Anthropic releases Claude Duet, a consumer‑friendly AI work assistant

Claude Duet is Anthropic’s newest AI agent aimed at consumers who want help with work without writing code. The author tested it for a week while juggling a busy travel and work schedule.

🔍 Overview

  • Claude Duet is positioned as a consumer‑friendly, work‑focused AI agent.
  • It follows earlier Anthropic agents: Claude Code (a coding agent) → Claude Cowork (more consumer‑friendly) → Claude Duet (most consumer‑friendly and work‑oriented).
  • Other recent agents mentioned in the landscape are Instinct’s text‑based assistant, Meta’s Muse, and OpenAI’s Dots.

⚙️ How it works

  • Users connect productivity and chat services (email, calendar, Google Docs, Slack). Duet then scans the data and surfaces suggestions as swipeable cards, similar to a “to‑do list Tinder.”
  • Each morning Duet greets the user, highlights key items (e.g., packing for a video shoot), and proposes to‑dos with offers to draft messages or add agenda items.
  • By accessing a biweekly staff‑meeting summary email and Slack, Duet linked a meeting comment to a direct Slack message.
  • Access to a shared Google Doc let Duet identify the user’s manager for weekly 1:1 meetings.

📋 Key Details

  • Design – Cheery, minimalist Claude design; app described as consumer‑friendly and approachable.
  • Platform – Available as a standalone app, now fully supports the iPhone Duo.
  • Interaction style – Swipe left/right on suggestion cards; drafted messages are tagged “sent with Claude.”
  • Personalization – Mirrors the user’s writing habits (e.g., all‑lowercase style) and occasionally adds playful asides.
  • Data usage – Operates on data the user opts‑in to share; Anthropic notes ongoing testing of its judgment about when to message.

🚀 Availability

  • Claude Duet is a “research preview.”
  • Access limited to Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the United States, with a waitlist for additional users.
  • Intended for “professionals and small business owners,” not for casual tasks like ordering food.

💡 Why it matters

  • Compared to Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots, Duet is described as “even more focused on work.”
  • It pushes the idea that AI agents can be useful for non‑programmers by handling everyday professional workflows.
  • The swipe‑card interface and daily brief aim to make AI assistance feel like a natural extension of existing productivity tools.

📊 Comparison to other agents

Agent Primary focus
Claude Duet Consumer‑friendly work assistance
Claude Cowork More consumer‑friendly than Claude Code
Claude Code Coding assistance
Instinct Text‑based assistant
Meta Muse Help with buying things
OpenAI Dots Work‑oriented assistant

#Anthropic #ClaudeDuet #AIagents #Productivity

Source: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful

item.title: Google launches Tabletop, an AI‑powered collaborative planning tool
item.description:
Google launches Tabletop, an AI‑powered collaborative planning tool

Google has introduced Tabletop, an experimental AI tool that lets users create customized collaborative hubs for personal planning.

🔍 Overview

  • Tabletop is a new experimental AI tool from Google.
  • It generates personalized interactive tools such as savings trackers, chore charts, event plans, and more.
  • The interface resembles workplace management apps like Asana and Monday, but is aimed at personal use.

🧩 How it works

  • Users add links, files, and ideas, then prompt @tabletop or choose a starter template.
  • “Just add in your links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets,” Google Labs design and engineering lead Roman Nurik said in the blog post.
  • Once a space is ready, an invite link can be shared in a group chat for simultaneous collaboration, similar to a Google Doc.
  • “Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time like a Google Doc.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Customizable collaborative spaces for personal planning needs.
  • Supports creating tools like savings trackers, chore charts, event plans.
  • Visual style similar to Asana/Monday with built‑in AI generation.

🚀 Availability

  • Tabletop is in beta and accessible via a waitlist.
  • Currently limited to users aged 18 + in the United States.
  • The age requirement may be temporary while Tabletop is in public testing.

💡 Why it matters

  • Offers a less formal alternative to workplace software for families and friends.
  • Enables real‑time shared planning without needing separate apps.

#GoogleAI #Productivity #Collaboration #AIExperiment

Source: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps

item.title: Apple pushes Siri toward agentic AI with new app integration and fine‑grained controls
item.description:
Apple pushes Siri toward agentic AI with new app integration and fine‑grained controls

Apple is updating Siri to become more agentic, adding fine‑grained control over its own apps and integration with third‑party services.

🔍 Overview

  • Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap.
  • Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, but the company acknowledges it is not keeping pace with rivals.
  • Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic and to enable ongoing tasks rather than single‑step commands.

⚙️ Upcoming Features

  • Fine‑grained control of first‑party apps – Siri will be able to rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Expected with iOS 27.3.
  • Third‑party app integration – Siri will place orders through Grubhub, book reservations through OpenTable, and similar actions. Expected in the Spring following iOS 27.3.

📅 Timeline

Feature Expected Release
First‑party app control (Photos, Safari) iOS 27.3
Third‑party app integration (Grubhub, OpenTable) Spring after iOS 27.3

💡 Why it matters

  • Competitors such as OpenAI’s Dots, Meta’s Muse, and Grok can keep track of goals and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every step.
  • Apple aims to give Siri similar agentic capabilities, allowing it to perform ongoing tasks and manage objectives, a direction the company may reach as early as next year.

#Apple #Siri #AIagents #VoiceAssistants

Source: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic

item.title: Meta launches real‑time voice mode and expressive avatars for Muse AI agent
item.description:
Meta launches real‑time voice mode and expressive avatars for Muse AI agent

Meta announced that its Muse AI agent now supports real‑time voice conversations with expressive animated avatars.

🔍 Overview

  • Muse AI agent now has a voice mode.
  • Voice mode includes selectable voices and expressive avatars that animate while chatting.

🧩 How it works

  • Users can talk to Muse in real time; the avatar at the top of the conversation animates in time with the words.
  • The voice tone can be changed by asking the agent what you want or by browsing options in the avatar settings.
  • In brief tests, the agent responds quickly over voice, with occasional pauses while it looks up information, similar to text‑chat behavior.

⚙️ Key details

  • The feature has been rolled out to users in the United States and is available on the iOS app (tested while writing this article).
  • Avatars are customizable; one user set the avatar to look like Mark Zuckerberg, noting the experience feels “quite weird.”
  • The voice cannot be made to sound exactly like Mark Zuckerberg.

🚀 Availability

  • Voice mode and expressive avatars are rolling out now in the US for the Muse app.
  • Meta says they will arrive “soon” for its AI glasses.
  • The features will also be included in the forthcoming Muse Charm gadget, which is expected to ship later this year.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables spoken interaction with a personal AI agent in real time.
  • Adds visual expressiveness through animated avatars that move in sync with speech.

#Meta #MuseAI #VoiceAI #AIavatars

Source: Muse has a voice mode now

item.title: AT&T Integrates Gemini AI Into Connected Life Home Security System
item.description:
AT&T Integrates Gemini AI Into Connected Life Home Security System

AT&T has integrated its Connected Life smart home security system with Gemini for Home, making it the first home security product to support Google Home Premium. This update enables a suite of Gemini-powered features that allow users to summarize home events and search through video history using natural language.

🔍 Overview

The integration leverages Google’s Gemini-powered Home APIs, which allow smart home brands and developers to build AI-driven features into their devices. This development follows the initial launch of the Connected Life system last December, which AT&T created in partnership with Google and Abode.

⚙️ Key details

The system now supports several AI-enhanced capabilities for monitoring home activity:

  • Natural Language Search: Users can query recorded footage with specific questions such as “What dug up the yard last night?” or “Who let the dogs out?”
  • Detailed Event Descriptions: Gemini can provide specific details about captured events, such as identifying who delivered a package and how many items they dropped off.
  • Activity Summaries: Users can review daily summaries of activity occurring both inside and outside the home.
  • Automated Arming: AT&T is adding the ability to automatically arm or disarm the security system based on the user’s proximity to their home.

🚀 Availability

These Gemini-powered features are not available on all tiers of service. Access to these tools requires:

  • Plan: AT&T’s professional Connected Life monitoring plan.
  • Cost: $29.99 per month.

💡 Why it matters

While AT&T is the first to integrate these Google Home Premium features, other companies are expected to follow. ADT has also hinted at plans to bring Gemini for Home features into its own security systems.

#ATT #Gemini #SmartHome #HomeSecurity #GoogleHome

Source: Gemini for Home now plugs into AT&T’s smart security system

item.title: Google launches Universal AI‑Powered Shopping Cart in the US
item.description:
Google launches Universal AI‑Powered Shopping Cart in the US

Google’s intelligent AI shopping cart is finally here, arriving just in time for Black Friday and seasonal holiday spending.

🛒 Overview

  • The Universal Cart tool Google previewed at its I/O event in May is now rolling out in the US across the Gemini app and Google Search.
  • It is described as a “universal” digital cart that lets you save products from multiple retailers in a single unified space and works across different Google platforms.

⚙️ How it works

  • You can find and add a bunch of products using the Gemini app and Google Search AI Mode, and they’ll all be saved to the same cart.
  • The cart can send you notifications about price drops and restocks for items saved, sparing you from checking each retailer’s website individually, and can display any relevant promotional codes it finds.
  • You can choose to pay for items from the cart using Google Wallet, or transfer them to the merchant’s own cart so you can checkout with the retailer directly.
  • Together with Google Wallet, Universal Cart can also analyze the perks provided by each of your saved credit cards and help you choose the best payment method when purchasing.

📦 Features

  • Cross‑retailer storage – saves products from multiple merchants in one cart.
  • Multi‑platform access – available in Google Search, Gemini app, with planned integration for Gmail and YouTube (timeline not announced).
  • Price‑watch notifications – alerts for drops, restocks, and auto‑found promo codes.
  • Flexible checkout – pay via Google Wallet or move items to the merchant’s cart.
  • Credit‑card perk analysis – suggests the optimal card using Google Wallet data.

🚀 Availability

  • The rollout is currently in the United States and is first reaching Google Search and the Gemini app.

📈 Why it matters

  • The launch comes as competition in the AI‑assisted shopping space is heating up; rivals such as OpenAI and Meta have launched agentic AI assistants that can shop online on the user’s behalf.
  • Shopify recently announced it is opening its platform to allow more AI agents to browse and purchase from Shopify listings.
  • Big Tech players are entering this race on the bet that the future of online shopping involves having a robot do most of the work for you.

#Google #AIShopping #UniversalCart #Ecommerce

Source: Google launches its ‘universal’ online shopping cart ahead of the holidays

item.title: Google pushes Android 17 developer preview with battery and privacy enhancements
item.description:
Google pushes Android 17 developer preview with battery and privacy enhancements

The Android ecosystem is busy this weekend as Google released a fresh update to the Android 17 developer preview, focusing on better battery life, background‑process control, and new privacy tweaks.

🔍 Overview

  • Android 17 developer preview arrives with a revamped battery settings menu.
  • Users can now see which background services consume the most power.
  • A new Private Space folder lets you hide specific apps from the app drawer without uninstalling them.
  • Notification snooze lets you silence alerts for one or two hours.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Battery Management
    • Revamped battery settings menu.
    • Visibility of power‑hungry background services.
  • App Privacy
    • Hide apps in the Private Space folder.
    • Google aims to help users find apps that behave badly.
  • Notification Control
    • Swipe a notification to the side for a snooze option.

📱 Additional Android Updates

  • Google Maps – Minor update adds the ability to save multiple custom routes as home‑screen shortcuts.
  • Google Photos – Refresh includes a faster search index for quicker object and person searches.
  • Security Patch – October security patch released for all supported Pixel devices, fixing three major flaws that could allow unauthorized media‑file access. Other manufacturers (OnePlus, Motorola) expected to roll it out by mid‑next week.

🚀 Availability

  • The Android 17 preview is now available for developers.
  • Google plans to open the beta to more devices soon.
  • Reminder: Back up your data before installing major system updates; keeping copies of photos and documents is always wise.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Improved battery visibility helps users extend device runtime.
  • Enhanced privacy controls give users more granular app management.
  • Faster search in Google Photos and custom route shortcuts in Maps streamline everyday tasks.
  • The October security patch addresses critical vulnerabilities, reinforcing device security across the ecosystem.

#android #android17 #mobileupdates #privacy #security

Source: Android Daily News: October 10, 2026 – Latest Updates and Releases - thetechpapa

item.title: Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots: New Consumer‑Friendly AI Agents Roll Out
item.description:
Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots: New Consumer‑Friendly AI Agents Roll Out

Meta and OpenAI have just launched the next wave of consumer‑friendly AI agents – Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots – each wrapped in a cute animated mascot and positioned as always‑on personal assistants. The releases prompt a fresh look at what autonomous agents can do today and whether users are willing to hand over sensitive data.

🔍 Overview

  • Muse and Dots are marketed to both mainstream users and businesses.
  • Both agents are described as “always‑on, autonomous AI agents” that can act on your behalf without constant supervision.
  • The launches follow a broader timeline:
    • 2022: “year of ideation” for agents.
    • 2023: “year of deployment” – companies began testing and learning.
    • 2026: the start of truly useful consumer agents, according to observers.

🤖 What Is an AI Agent?

  • An agent is “an AI model wrapped in a harness that lets it use a computer.”
  • It can complete multi‑step, complex tasks on your behalf without you hand‑holding it the whole time.
  • Typical use cases mentioned include restaurant reservations, inbox triage, flight bookings, buying gifts, and more sophisticated workflows.

📦 Product Details

Agent Company Cost Specialist Variants Mascot Style
Muse Meta Free None listed Adorable animated mascot (launched weeks after Meta Connect)
Dots OpenAI Paid Marketing, Legal, Accounting Cute animated mascot (new agent platform)

🔧 Capabilities

  • Everyday tasks: restaurant reservations, inbox triage, flight and dinner bookings, gift purchases.
  • Business workflows: OpenAI offers specialist Dots for marketing, legal work, and accounting.
  • Always‑on operation: Both agents are designed to run continuously and act without requiring a separate app or phone.

⚠️ Privacy & Security Concerns

  • The agents require access to personal data such as credit‑card information, email inboxes, and other hard‑drive files.
  • Earlier homebrew agents like OpenClaw demonstrated privacy flaws; Peter Steinberger’s OpenClaw tool was “actually useful” but “had a lot of privacy and security issues.”
  • OpenAI hired Steinberger, leading to the development of Dots.
  • Meta, lacking its own frontier model, relies on product distribution strengths but still raises the question: Can you trust Meta’s Muse or OpenAI’s Dots to run your life?
  • The broader conversation centers on whether users are comfortable handing over such data to an autonomous agent that could operate without a traditional app.

📅 Timeline Highlights

  • 2022: Ideation phase for AI agents.
  • 2023: Deployment phase – companies tested early versions.
  • Early 2026: Surge in Mac Mini sales linked to homebrew OpenClaw setups.
  • Weeks after Meta Connect (2026): Muse announced.
  • A few weeks later (2026): OpenAI announced Dots.

The launch of Muse and Dots marks a clear move from experimental tools toward everyday AI assistants, while the privacy debate remains unresolved.

#Meta #OpenAI #AIagents #Privacy

Source: How Meta got ahead of OpenAI in the AI agent race

item.title: Meta Launches Muse AI Assistant Designed to Watch Learn and Act
item.description:
Meta Launches Muse AI Assistant Designed to Watch Learn and Act

Meta has launched Muse, a new AI assistant designed to watch, learn, and act on your behalf. The company promises a future where artificial intelligence helps manage everything from shopping and bookings to emails and daily tasks.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Watch, Learn, and Act: Muse is built to watch, learn, and take actions on behalf of the user.
  • Task Management: Meta promises the assistant will help manage daily tasks, emails, shopping, and bookings.
  • Wearable Integration: The assistant is designed to remain with users at all times via wearable devices.

💡 Why It Matters

The launch of Muse has initiated discussions regarding whether the assistant is a helpful digital companion or a step forward in Big Tech’s push into personal lives. On the program AI Decoded, presenter Christian Fraser, AI technology critic Ed Zitron, and AI consumer tech expert Ben Hatton explored the implications of the technology, including:

  • Whether Muse is a breakthrough in personal AI or a gateway to unprecedented data collection.
  • What users may be giving up in exchange for convenience.
  • Whether the technology risks giving Meta unprecedented influence over everyday decisions.
  • Whether Muse will become an indispensable assistant or Meta’s “Trojan horse.”

#Meta #Muse #AIAgents #AIDecoded #Privacy

Source: BBC News - AI Decoded, Is Muse Meta’s new ‘AI Trojan Horse’?

item.title: Anthropic Faces Class Action Lawsuit Over Allegedly Misleading Claude Max Subscription Limits
item.description:
Anthropic Faces Class Action Lawsuit Over Allegedly Misleading Claude Max Subscription Limits

Anthropic is facing legal scrutiny after subscribers accused the company of deceptively marketing its premium Claude Max AI subscription tier. The expanded class action lawsuit alleges that Anthropic misrepresented usage limits, leaving customers feeling misled about the value of their $100-$200 monthly subscriptions.

🔍 Overview

Claude subscribers claim Anthropic obscured critical usage restrictions for its Max plan, advertising “5x” or “20x” greater capacity than the base Pro tier while burying strict session-based limits in hard-to-find fine print. The lawsuit argues this constitutes false advertising.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Pricing Tiers:
    Plan Cost Advertised Usage Actual Limit (Alleged)
    Max 5x $100/month 5× Pro capacity 5-hour sessions with weekly cap
    Max 20x $200/month 20× Pro capacity Same session/weekly constraints
  • Hidden Limitations: The complaint states session limits were added months after launch and required clicking multiple hyperlinks to discover, with one user comparing it to “a bigger gas tank with a restricted fuel pump.”
  • Corporate Priority: Anthropic deprioritized other applications (e.g., OpenClaw) to focus on power users, yet allegedly obscured Max plan constraints.

💬 Key Quotes

  • Reddit User: “The weekly allowance is what the pricing page makes you think you’re buying. The rolling 5-hour window is what actually controls whether you can work.”
  • Attorney Monica Vaca: “People see that they are going to get this dramatically expanded usage… but when they sign up, they are surprised that they’re not getting the usage that they thought they were getting.”
  • Anthropic’s Defense: “Accessing this clarifying information required nothing more than clicking hyperlinks… the digital equivalent of flipping a product over to read the back label.”

⚖️ Legal Context

  • Filed by former FTC attorneys Monica Vaca and Kati Daffan (38 combined years at the agency), the lawsuit emphasizes false advertising principles: “You can’t lie when you’re marketing a product.”
  • Plaintiffs argue Anthropic violated consumer protection laws through deliberate obscurity of terms, forcing a “buyer beware” dynamic for premium subscribers.

💡 Why It Matters

This case represents a rare legal challenge to AI industry pricing practices, highlighting tensions between profit models and transparency. As AI tools become essential for professionals, unclear usage policies risk eroding trust—particularly when upgrades cost $100-$200 monthly. The outcome could pressure companies to simplify terms and align marketing with actual user experience.

#Anthropic #ClaudeAI #Lawsuit #AIEthics #ConsumerRights

Source: A new class action lawsuit questions whether Anthropic broke the law by misleading power users
